title: ci(workflows): route every pnpm bootstrap through one retried, self-describing setup step
body:
Fixes #8099

A Corepack fetch of the pinned pnpm tarball died inside undici ten seconds into a job, reddening the **required** check `README Export Check` on a one-file prose diff, before any gate logic ran. `rerun_failed_jobs` on the same head (`3916de68`) turned it green with no code change — same commit, same gate, opposite conclusion. That control is the card's, and this PR does not re-derive it.

## Preconditions, re-measured on `origin/main` `4dc80d0fc`

| # | Claim | Verdict | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15 workflows carry `corepack enable` | ⚠️ **FALSIFIED as a count of workflows that RUN it** | 15 files *mention* the string; only **13 files / 18 executable `run:` steps** invoke it. See below. |
| 2 | `README Export Check` is a required context, and the `merge_group` floor derives from that list | **CONFIRMED** | `scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs:177` in `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`, mapped to `readme-exports.yml` at `:134` (the card said `:176`; the tree reads `:177` today). The derivation is stated at `:146-148` — "this list is what `merge-queue-reporting.test.ts` derives the `merge_group` subscription floor from" — and echoed at `readme-exports.yml:38`. |
| 3 | `actions/setup-node` with `cache: 'pnpm'` is present in the failing workflow | **CONFIRMED** | `readme-exports.yml:78-82`. It caches the pnpm **store**; the corepack-downloaded pnpm **binary** is a different artifact and is not cached by it. |
| 4 | The 60-minute stall property is stated in four files | **CONFIRMED** | `readme-exports.yml:47-48`, verbatim: *"A required check that does not report on a queue build stalls the queue until the ruleset's 60-minute timeout fails it"*. Also `changeset-presence.yml:45`/`:62`, `ci.yml:158`, `control-bytes.yml:48`. |
| 5 | Are the sites uniform? | **FALSIFIED — three shapes** | See "Not uniform" below. |

### Precondition 1, in full — the number is 13, not 15

`grep -rl 'corepack enable' .github/workflows/` returns **15** files. Three of the 21 occurrences are inside YAML **comments**, in two files:

- `changelog.yml:97` — a note saying that *if* a pnpm-dependent step is ever added there, corepack setup must be added ahead of it.
- `dependabot-auto-merge.yml:93` and `:109` — the record of **#6392**, which *removed* the step from that job because nothing in it calls pnpm: *"an unexplained two-line 'just in case' setup with no consumer is exactly the residue this issue is about"*.

Reading `run:` bodies instead: **13 files, 18 steps**. Controls, same run: `grep -rl 'run: pnpm install'` → 12 files (the pattern class hits); `grep -rn 'run: corepack disable'` → exit 1 (a same-class absent token). And an independent measurement of the same set from parsed `run:` bodies: **13 workflows invoke `pnpm`, 13 invoke `corepack`, and the two sets are identical** — no workflow is in one and not the other.

⇒ Applying the fix to "all 15" would have meant putting a pnpm download into two jobs that deliberately have none, one of them against a recorded ruling. **The declared breadth is met at 18/18 executable sites across 13 files, with those two named as exceptions and left untouched.**

### Precondition 5 — not uniform, and the non-uniformity is the point

`corepack enable` only writes shims. **The first pnpm *invocation* is what downloads** — and that differs per site:

| Shape | Sites | Where the download actually landed |
|---|---|---|
| A: `pnpm --version` immediately after | 10 (`ci.yml` ×6, `lint.yml`, `shadcn-check.yml`, `performance-budget.yml`, `changeset-release.yml`) | a step named "Verify pnpm version" |
| B: straight to `actions/setup-node` with `cache: 'pnpm'` | 7 (`readme-exports.yml`, `node-esm-load-gate.yml`, `live-e2e.yml`, `spec-range-floors.yml`, `published-dist-gate.yml`, `doc-snippet-types.yml`, `skill-examples.yml`) | **inside the third-party action's own step**, via its store probe |
| C: no pnpm cache, no install | 1 (`docs-route-eager-closure.yml`) | inside the gate's own step, reading as the gate failing |

⚠️ This falsifies the shape of the naive fix: **a retry wrapped around `corepack enable` would have protected nothing in 7 of the 18 sites**, because in Shape B `corepack enable` is not the step that downloads. The failing workflow is Shape B.

## Direction chosen: ③ retry — knowingly, and it is not bare ③

⛔ Not ② `pnpm/action-setup`. **It would be a maintainer-floor decision, so I did not take it.** No workflow in this repository has ever used it, it is the only candidate that adds a third-party action dependency, and the repo actively documents its absence: `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md:2343` and two changesets say so, and `scripts/__tests__/doc-version-claims.test.ts:2205` pins the spelling as an out-of-ledger boundary.

⛔ Not ① cache-the-tarball, and the reasoning is on the four axes below. `cache: 'pnpm'` is **not** an answer and was not treated as one: it caches the store, not the binary.

**③, stated knowingly as triage required** — implemented as `scripts/ci-setup-pnpm.sh`, called from all 18 sites, which does two things a bare retry does not:

1. **Makes the download explicit and single-homed.** The registry read now happens in one named step in every workflow instead of leaking into `actions/setup-node` or into a gate's own step. Without this the retry would be a no-op in 7 sites.
2. **Bounds and retries it** — 4 attempts, 5s/10s/15s backoff (30s worst case, against a 60-minute queue stall), each retry emitting a `::warning::` that names the toolchain as the culprit.

### Four-axis analysis

**实际业务需求.** Measured, not speculative: one real occurrence with the same-head re-run control, and an exposure of 13 workflows measured on the tree rather than assumed. What is *not* measured is a rate — one sighting. ③ costs one step per site and zero steady-state seconds; ① would buy protection against an outage class that has not been observed here, at a much larger standing cost. The measured need is "absorb a transient read", and that is exactly what ③ absorbs.

**项目长远合理性.** ① pins `~/.cache/node/corepack`, a Corepack *internal* layout this repo does not own, into 18 places, plus a cache key that must track `packageManager` or silently stop helping — a cache whose path drifts is a **silent** no-op, the phantom-gate shape this repo repeatedly refuses. ③ adds no new dependency and no new failure surface, and it is not a workaround for a defect of ours: there is no upstream contract being papered over, only an inherently unreliable network read handled the standard way. And ① would still need ③ underneath it for every cold path. One home, one mechanism.

**防 AI 写代码犯错.** This is where ③-as-implemented is strongest. Contract-first, not consumer-tolerance: the wiring test **refuses** a workflow that spells `corepack` in a `run:` step and **refuses** one that invokes `pnpm` without the setup — a declaration enforced mechanically rather than a convention re-swept by hand. Before this, "the workflow needs pnpm" was implicit and every new workflow re-derived it. Note that ① would have made this *worse*: a cache step that silently misses is precisely the tolerant-fallback shape.

**创业阶段不扩散需求.** ③ is one script and one line per site. ① is a caching subsystem plus version derivation across 18 sites, for an outage class not yet seen here. Focus principle favours the minimum that covers the measured failure.

⚠️ **Where the axes conflict, stated rather than resolved:** on 项目长远合理性 alone, triage is right that ③ does not remove the registry from the hot path — ① is the only direction that survives a sustained outage. I am not claiming otherwise. I weighed that against the silent-no-op risk of a corepack-internal cache path replicated 18 times, and against the fact that ① cannot stand without ③ anyway. **If the maintainer wants outage-survival rather than blip-absorption, that is a further card and ① layers on top of this without undoing it.**

## ⛔ What this does NOT cover

- **The registry dependency remains.** Every cold job still reads `registry.npmjs.org` once. A sustained npm outage still reds all 13 workflows. Only a cached-tarball approach survives that; this is deliberately not that.
- **It bounds, it does not eliminate.** A blip outlasting 4 attempts still fails the job.
- **It changes nothing about the consequence of a red** — the 60-minute queue-stall property is untouched. What changes is the probability of entering it via this failure class.
- **The 10 Shape-A `Verify pnpm version` steps are left in place.** They are now guaranteed cache hits and cost ~nothing; removing them is out of this card's scope.
- **The job-log egress obstacle is untouched** (see below) — not this card's to fix.

## ⭐ Self-evidence: is the failure readable from the step name alone?

**Yes, for this failure class — and that is a change.** Previously a reader saw `Verify pnpm version`, `Setup Node.js` or the gate's own step name go red, and in Shape B a `Setup Node.js` failure is genuinely ambiguous. Now every site fails under:

> **Enable Corepack and download the pinned pnpm**

which names the toolchain fetch and nothing about the diff. The `::error::` annotation surfaced on the checks page says so in words: *"This step reads registry.npmjs.org and judges nothing about the diff under test."*

⚠️ **The honest boundary:** this makes *this* failure class self-evident. It does not make every red self-evident, and it does not remove the underlying obstacle — `productionresultssa11.blob.core.windows.net` is still egress-denied for container seats, so REST log download still returns HTTP 000 and only MCP `get_job_logs` answers. An agent facing a red in some *other* step still pays that cost. The next agent hitting *this* one should not have to fetch a log at all.

## Breadth is now mechanical, not a one-time sweep

`scripts/__tests__/ci-setup-pnpm-wiring.test.ts` pins four properties, each with an anti-vacuity control in the same run:

1. the script exists and is executable;
2. **no `run:` step spells `corepack` directly** — reading `run:` *bodies*, so the two comment-only mentions stay unjudged (and are asserted still present, so the rule cannot pass by an emptied corpus);
3. **every workflow invoking `pnpm` calls the setup** — the direction a 14th workflow fails;
4. **every job calling it checks out first** — the script is a repo file.

This is the part that answers triage's "fixing the one that failed makes the next occurrence harder to recognise": a 14th workflow cannot now be written onto the unprotected path.

## ⚠️ What I could and could not verify locally

**Cannot be verified without a CI run, and I claim no green I did not see:**

- That the retry absorbs a **real** undici/TLS abort from `registry.npmjs.org`. The observed failure cannot be reproduced on demand; what is proven is that the loop retries a failing read and succeeds when a later read succeeds.
- That `bash scripts/ci-setup-pnpm.sh` behaves as expected on the GitHub runner image (PATH placement of the Corepack shims after `actions/setup-node` switches Node).
- Any workflow-level behaviour at all: triggers, `merge_group` legs, step ordering as executed.

**Verified locally, with the command and its real reading:**

| Check | Exit | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| `bash scripts/ci-setup-pnpm.sh --self-test` | 0 | 6/6 — no retry on a green first read (1 call); absorbs 2 transient failures (3 calls); gives up at the budget (status 1, 3 calls); plus the stub-really-failed control and both annotation assertions |
| **Ablation** (`attempt + 1` → `attempt + ATTEMPTS`, from the committed tree) | 1 | The two retry cases go red, the first-read case stays green — the direction predicted. Restore proved by bytes: `git hash-object` = `82ca796…` = `git rev-parse HEAD:scripts/ci-setup-pnpm.sh`, marker count 0, `git diff HEAD` empty, self-test back to 0 |
| YAML parse of all 13 changed workflows | 0 | every file parses and yields a `jobs:` mapping (`ci.yml` 7 jobs/80 steps, etc.) |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/` | 0 | **126 files passed, 2 skipped; 3691 tests passed** — includes `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts`, `doc-version-claims.test.ts`, `bash32-floor-wiring.test.ts` and the two "no corepack here" pins |
| `pnpm check:action-ref-convention` | 0 | 109 refs in 35 files, 0 off-convention; control `actions/checkout` present: true |
| `pnpm check:bash32-floor` | 0 | **13** tracked shell files (11→…→13 after staging; the pre-staging run read 12 and did **not** include the new script — it uses `git ls-files`, so that first green was not a measurement) |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | 0 | 6854 tracked text files (6851 before staging) |
| `pnpm check:shell-escape-residue` | 0 | 5/5 roots resolved, 206 files / 1312 fences |
| `pnpm check:action-forward-parity` | 0 | 5 surfaces, 39 runtime-read keys |
| `pnpm docs:check-links` | 0 | valid across 17 scan roots — covers the new `#toolchain-setup-scriptsci-setup-pnpmsh` anchor, whose slug was computed with the repo's own `scripts/github-slug.mjs` |
| `pnpm check:doc-fences` | 0 | 227 documents |
| `pnpm check-changeset-presence` | 0 | 14 files changed, 0 published source, 1 changeset added |
| `pnpm exec eslint scripts/__tests__/ci-setup-pnpm-wiring.test.ts` | 0 | clean (first run found 1 error, an unused `no-bitwise` disable; fixed in the second commit) |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | 0 | and `tsc --listFiles` confirms the new test file **is in that program** (count 1) — so this is a measurement, not an `exclude`d green |

⛔ Not run locally: the repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full `pnpm test`. Those are CI's runs.

## Changeset

Empty frontmatter, per AGENTS.md §9 — CI and docs only, no published package source and no manifest contract field moved. `check-changeset-presence.mjs` confirms: *"0 of them published source of a package the release covers"*.

## Files touched

- `scripts/ci-setup-pnpm.sh` (new) — the shared setup, its rationale, and its self-test
- `scripts/__tests__/ci-setup-pnpm-wiring.test.ts` (new) — the breadth pin
- 13 workflows, 18 sites — `.github/workflows/{ci,lint,live-e2e,readme-exports,shadcn-check,node-esm-load-gate,spec-range-floors,published-dist-gate,doc-snippet-types,skill-examples,docs-route-eager-closure,performance-budget,changeset-release}.yml`
- `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` — new **Toolchain Setup** section; the living workflow example updated (it showed `- run: corepack enable` and would otherwise have become the fossil that page warns about)
- `.changeset/8099-corepack-pnpm-download.md`

## 维护者速读(草稿)

**改了什么** — CI 里 13 个 workflow、18 处 `corepack enable` 全部改为调用一个共享脚本 `scripts/ci-setup-pnpm.sh`;该脚本先 `corepack enable`,再显式地把 pinned pnpm 下载下来,失败时最多重试 4 次(5s/10s/15s 退避)。另加一个测试锁死"覆盖面",并更新 CI 文档。

**为什么改** — pnpm 不在 runner 上,每个 job 都要从 npm registry 下载一次。这次下载在 undici 里崩了,把**必需检查** `README Export Check` 在一个只改了一个 markdown 文件的 PR 上刷红。同一个 commit 重跑就绿了。这个检查是必需上下文,`merge_group` 门槛又是从那份清单推导的,所以在合并队列这条腿上代价是 60 分钟排队停滞,不是"重跑一次"。

**风险与代价(含回滚)** — 风险面是 CI 本身:workflow 改动无法在本地证明,只有真跑一次 CI 才知道。已在本地验证的是 YAML 全部可解析、脚本自测通过(含一次消融证明它真的会失败)、以及所有读 workflow / shell / 文档的门禁都绿。回滚成本低:revert 本 PR 即可,没有任何运行时代码、发布包或契约被改动。⛔ 有意**没有**选"缓存 pnpm 二进制"那条路——它要把 Corepack 的内部缓存路径钉进 18 个地方,一旦路径漂移就是静默失效;那条路可以在此基础上叠加,不需要先撤销本 PR。

**席位意见** — (留空,待席位定稿)

**你要做的** — 确认方向选择:本 PR 走的是 triage 三条路里的第 ③ 条(重试),是**明知代价**选的,并未消除对 npm registry 的依赖。若你要的是"registry 挂了也能跑",那需要另开一张卡走缓存方案。除此之外无需操作。
